However, Musk dropped out after two days and, with his brother [Kimbal](Kimbal_Musk "Kimbal Musk"), co-founded online [city guide](City_guide "City guide") software company <Zip2>. The startup was acquired by <Compaq> for $307 million in 1999, and with $12 million of the money he made, that same year Musk co-founded [X.com](X.com_(bank) "X.com (bank)"), a [direct bank](Direct_bank "Direct bank"). X.com merged with <Confinity> in 2000 to form <PayPal>.

In 2002, [eBay](EBay "EBay") acquired PayPal for $1.5 billion, and that same year, with $100 million of the money he made, Musk founded SpaceX, a [spaceflight](Spaceflight "Spaceflight") services company. He became its chairman and product architect, assuming the position of CEO in 2008. In 2006, Musk helped create <SolarCity>, a solar-energy company that was acquired by Tesla in 2016 and became [Tesla Energy](Tesla_Energy "Tesla Energy"). In 2013, he proposed a [hyperloop](Hyperloop "Hyperloop") high-speed [vactrain](Vactrain "Vactrain") transportation system. In 2015, he co-founded OpenAI, a nonprofit [artificial intelligence](Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") research company. [Musk has expressed views](Views_of_Elon_Musk "Views of Elon Musk") that have made him a polarizing figure. His [Twitter ownership](Twitter_under_Elon_Musk "Twitter under Elon Musk") has been similarly controversial, including laying off a large number of employees, an increase in [hate speech](Hate_speech "Hate speech") on the platform, and changes to [Twitter Blue verification](Twitter_Blue_verification_controversy "Twitter Blue verification controversy") were criticized. In 2018, the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission](U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") (SEC) sued him for falsely tweeting that he had secured funding for a private takeover of Tesla. <IBM>, the leading supplier of computer equipment to commercial enterprises at the time, approached Microsoft in July 1980 concerning software for its upcoming personal computer, the [IBM PC](IBM_PC "IBM PC"),[[60]](Bill_Gates#cite_note-bunnell1982febmar-62) after Gates's mother, [Mary Maxwell Gates](Mary_Maxwell_Gates "Mary Maxwell Gates"), mentioned Microsoft to [John Opel](John_Opel "John Opel"), IBM's then <CEO>.[[61]](Bill_Gates#cite_note-63) IBM first proposed that Microsoft write the BASIC interpreter. It was the prestige brought to Microsoft by IBM's adoption of their operating system that would be the origin of Microsoft's transformation from a small business to the leading software company in the world.
